description_full: Galderma Group AG operates as a dermatology company worldwide. The company delivers a science-based portfolio of brands and services for the dermatology market, including injectable aesthetics, dermatological skincare, and therapeutic dermatology. Its portfolio of flagship brands includes Azzalure, ALLUZIENCE, Dysport, Restylane, Restylane Skinboosters, Sculptra, Cetaphil, ALASTIN, Soolantra, Epiduo, Epiduo Forte, Differin, AKLIEF, Oracea, Metvix, NEMLUVIO, Relfydess, Benzac, and Loceryl in therapeutic dermatology. The company was founded in 1981 and is headquartered in Zug, Switzerland.

financial_summary: GALDERMA GROUP AG is a large-cap healthcare business with a $53.3B market cap on $5.2B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +2.0pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 69% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.0B in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.93× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.6× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 5.0×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.8%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
